adele (support): i pulled the proxy and edge logs for the time window; no 5xx on our side. the edge returned 200s and flushed chunks but our write path shows repeated `EAGAIN` and then a `SIGPIPE` / `EPIPE` on the send. here's a snippet from our edge:```

tanvi (eng-sre): that pattern screams slow consumer / socket buffer fill. typical causes: (1) client is reading very slowly (intentionally slow reader), (2) an intermediate proxy (customer's or ours) is buffering and then timing out, (3) nginx or cloud LB has buffering/gzip enabled so flushes never reach client.

jon (eng-runtime): agree. can you ask customer for a minimal repro? ideally curl with --no-buffer or a small python client that reads one byte/sec. also need their proxy (nginx/haproxy) config if possible.

adele (support): customer provided a repro script. they used a naive python SSE reader that sleeps between reads. reproduce command they gave:```
# slow-reader.sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import requests, time
for line in requests.get('https://api.redwood.example/events', stream=True, headers={'Accept':'text/event-stream'}).iter_lines():
    print(line)
    time.sleep(1.5)  # slow consumer
PY
```

adele (support): they also said they are behind a corporate proxy that adds `X-Accel-Buffering: yes` (nginx default).

jon (eng-runtime): that is important. Nginx buffer + gzip + proxy buffering will hold data until buffer full or end of response. with a slow consumer our kernel send buffer will fill and send() returns EAGAIN; our runtime retries a few times then bails (we currently have a ~5s total send retry window for streaming chunks before aborting to avoid resource stuck threads).

tanvi (eng-sre): mitigation steps: ask customer to set proxy header to disable buffering, e.g., `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx, and disable gzip / compression for SSE endpoints. on our side, we can loosen the send retry behaviour for connections coming from known enterprise proxies while we investigate.

jon (eng-runtime): also worth a quick repro from our side. i'll run a slow consumer against staging and see if we hit the same send path and reproduce the EAGAIN -> abort. share the curl command i'll use:
```
# fast server, slow client repro with curl
# server: staging endpoint /v1/stream-test
# client: slow reader
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://staging.api.redwood.example/v1/stream-test" | pv -qL 10  # limit throughput to 10 bytes/sec
```

jon (eng-runtime): preliminary run shows identical behaviour. after ~30s our write loop sees repeated EAGAIN, and because the runtime holds the request to avoid deadlocks it decides to close the connection to free the worker.

adele (support): customer asked whether this could cause billing spikes because they reconnect constantly — they saw increased request counts and higher token usage.

tanvi (eng-sre): yes it can. frequent reconnects cause the platform to process more handshake/initialization work and possibly re-send partial events. short-term: recommend customer increase client read window or use a backoff reconnect with resume semantics. we'll also add an internal note to track billing impact for retry storms.

jon (eng-runtime): quick patch suggestions: (1) allow configurable send retry window per route (support can enable for this customer), (2) emit a metric when a connection is aborted due to EAGAIN so we can correlate to customer re-connects. I'll open a ticket for the metric.

adele (support): customer tried setting `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and disabling gzip for the proxy. they confirm much more stable stream, no abrupt closes after 5+ minutes.

tanvi (eng-sre): excellent. please ask them to keep the slow-reader script running for a full hour and report back. i'll follow up to see if any pod is hitting high socket retry counts.
